description: The EXACT set of fields in each signed preimage, and what happens when that set is wrong. Fixes the one class of divergence every digest vector misses.
why_this_is_a_primitive: Every other vector answers 'given these inputs, are the bytes right?'. This one answers 'are these the right inputs at all?'. An implementation that omits a field from a signed preimage, or carries one the contract does not have, computes a PERFECTLY VALID digest over the wrong object. Its own tests pass, the digest vectors pass, and the divergence only surfaces when a second implementation verifies the signature and fails. Pinning the field set is the only check that fires at the producer.
how_to_use_this_vector: For each artifact below, compare the field set of your own type against `fields` — as a SET, both directions. Missing a field means you sign fewer bytes than the contract; carrying an extra means you sign more. Reading the fields you know is not enough: that only proves you can find yours, never that the contract has grown one you ignore.
ordering_note: `fields` is listed in the artifact's canonical order, which matters only for the insertion-ordered artifacts (marked below). For the JCS ones the order here is documentary — JCS sorts keys — but the SET is normative either way.

artifacts.byte_contract: see level1-binding/vectors.json for the exact bytes
see capacity-evidence/vectors.json for the exact bytes

artifacts.canonicalization: JCS (RFC 8785, sorted keys) over the no-signature view
artifacts.byte_contract: see operator-receipt/vectors.json for the exact bytes

shape_cases.name: exact field set
shape_cases.scenario: the producer's type carries precisely the fields listed for the artifact

shape_cases.name: missing field
shape_cases.scenario: a field in `fields` is absent from the producer's preimage
shape_cases.why: fewer bytes are signed than the contract fixes. The digest is internally consistent, so nothing local catches it — a verifier reconstructing the full preimage computes a different digest and the signature fails

shape_cases.name: extra field
shape_cases.scenario: the producer's preimage carries a field not in `fields`
shape_cases.why: THE case this vector exists for. More bytes are signed than the contract fixes. A consumer that reads only the fields it knows validates every one of them and still hashes a different object. No digest vector detects this, because each digest is correct for the object that was hashed

shape_cases.name: renamed field
shape_cases.scenario: a field carries the right value under a different key
shape_cases.why: a rename is simultaneously a missing field and an extra one; it is called out separately because it is what a refactor produces, and because a reader with a lenient default may see an empty value rather than an absent one

shape_cases.name: field present but empty
shape_cases.scenario: a required field is serialized as the empty string
shape_cases.why: an empty value is not an absent field: it changes the bytes without changing the shape, so the field-set check alone passes. Producers must refuse to sign a preimage with an unset required field rather than defaulting it

shape_cases.name: field order changed in an insertion-ordered artifact
shape_cases.scenario: the fields of level1-binding, capacity.evidence or a settlement preimage are emitted in a different order
shape_cases.why: these artifacts sign insertion order, not sorted order. The SET is unchanged, so a set comparison passes — this is why the byte vectors and this shape vector are both needed, and neither replaces the other

shape_cases.name: signature included in the signed view
shape_cases.scenario: operator.receipt/1 canonicalized WITH its signature field
shape_cases.why: the signature cannot be part of what it signs. The no-signature view is what gets canonicalized; including it is unsatisfiable and must fail at the producer

must_hold: each artifact's field set is compared in BOTH directions: no field missing, no field extra
a field set that matches is still not sufficient — the byte vectors fix order and encoding
an extra field in a signed preimage is a divergence even when every digest computed over it is correct
a required field present but empty is refused at the producer, not defaulted
operator.receipt/1 is canonicalized over the no-signature view
